html:
Ulpiana was a Roman city near today's Gračanica in central Kosovo, founded in the early 100s and named for the emperor Trajan, whose family name was Ulpius.

It grew rich on the silver and lead mines of the Dardanian hills, which the Romans worked on a large scale. It became a bishop's seat in the 300s. An earthquake ruined it in 518, and Justinian, born not far away, rebuilt it as Iustiniana Secunda. The city faded after the Slavs settled the Balkans around 600. Excavations have uncovered walls, a basilica and a cemetery. It is the main ancient site in Kosovo.
sum: Ulpiana was a Roman city near today's Gračanica in central Kosovo, founded in the early 100s and named for the emperor Trajan, whose family name was Ulpius.
